stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that watched the aggressive adult
The group that watched the quiet adult

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.01.

rows.group: The group that listened to an audiobook

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether nausea after a new taste produces an aversion to that taste. They recruited 40 laboratory rats and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Rats in one condition drank sweetened water and were then given an injection that causes mild nausea. Rats in the other condition drank sweetened water and were then given a harmless salt-water injection. The researchers then recorded the volume in milliliters of sweetened water that each rat drank the next day.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They hypothesized that the wording of the question would affect the remembered speed of the cars.

**Participants.** The sample was 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

**Results.** The group asked the question with the word 'smashed': mean estimated speed (km/h) = 66. The group asked the question with the word 'contacted': mean estimated speed (km/h) = 51. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?**

**Source A.** A survey of 1,200 teenagers found a correlation of r = +0.28 between hours of social media use per day and scores on a depression questionnaire. Teenagers who reported feeling lonely tended both to use social media more and to have higher depression scores.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 140 university students were randomly assigned either to limit social media use to 30 minutes a day for three weeks or to continue as usual. At the end, the limited group had a mean loneliness score of 38 and the usual-use group a mean of 45 (p = 0.03).

**Source C.** Researchers interviewed 40 teenagers about their experiences online. Many described feeling worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular; others described feeling supported by online friends who shared their interests.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the preoperational stage?

options.text: Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions
options.why: That describes the sensorimotor stage.

options.text: Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events
options.why: That describes the concrete operational stage.

options.text: Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically
options.why: Correct. This is what the preoperational stage means.

options.text: Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas
options.why: That describes the formal operational stage.

questions.explanation: The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it?

options.why: Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.
Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also test hypotheses.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also use numerical data.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: A brain scan shows strong activity in one structure when a person sees a threatening face. Which structure is it most likely to be?

options.why: The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
Correct. The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.
The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.

questions.explanation: The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.stem: A two-year-old says 'Daddy go' and 'more cookie'. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.
Correct. Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.

questions.explanation: Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a mental framework that organizes and interprets information?

options.why: Accommodation is the changing of an existing schema to fit new information.
A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.
Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.
Correct. A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.

questions.explanation: A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray?

options.why: The trichromatic theory is the theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue.
The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.
Correct. Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.explanation: Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an opioid?

options.text: A drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a depressant.

options.text: A drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a stimulant.

options.text: A drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive
options.why: Correct. This is what an opioid means.

options.text: A drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input
options.why: That describes a hallucinogen.

questions.explanation: An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.

questions.stem: In Pavlov's experiments, dogs salivated to food, and later to a tone that had been paired with food. Salivating to the food was which of the following?

options.why: The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
Correct. The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.explanation: The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The two groups had the same average result
options.why: The table shows different averages.

options.text: The results prove that every individual in the first group differed from every individual in the second
options.why: The table reports group averages, not individual scores.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant, so it is unlikely to be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

options.text: The difference between the groups is probably due to chance
options.why: A p value of 0.01 is below 0.05, so chance is an unlikely explanation.

questions.explanation: A p value below 0.05 means a difference this large would rarely occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated?

options.why: The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
Correct. Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.explanation: Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone?

options.why: A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.
Correct. A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.
Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.
Multiculturalism is the view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities.

questions.explanation: A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.stem: A female moth releases a chemical into the air that attracts males from far away. What is this chemical called?

options.why: Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Correct. A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.

questions.explanation: A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.

questions.stem: While dreaming, a man kicks and punches as he acts out his dream. Which sleep disorder does he most likely have?

options.why: Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.
Correct. REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.
Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.
Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.

questions.explanation: REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.

questions.stem: As well as obtaining permission from the parents, the researchers asked each child whether he or she was willing to take part. What is the child's agreement called?

options.why: Confidentiality is keeping data private.
Deception is misleading participants about the study.
Correct. Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.
Debriefing happens after the study.

questions.explanation: Minors cannot give legal consent, so they give assent and their parents give consent.

questions.stem: A tourist calls another country's eating customs 'wrong' because they differ from the customs at home. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.
Correct. Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.
An implicit attitude is an attitude that a person holds without being aware of it.
Prejudice is an unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members.

questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 5, 10, 2, 6, 8, 6, 19. What is the median of the scores?

options.why: Correct. Put the scores in order and take the middle one, the fourth of seven.
That is the mean.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 2, 5, 6, 6, 8, 10, 19. Put the scores in order and take the middle one, the fourth of seven. The one very high score pulls the mean (8) above the median (6), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes hoarding disorder?

options.text: The disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered
options.why: Correct. This is what hoarding disorder means.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event
options.why: That describes posttraumatic stress disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue)
options.why: That describes dissociative amnesia.

options.text: A repeated action that a person feels driven to perform to reduce anxiety
options.why: That describes a compulsion.

questions.explanation: Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.why: This is the independent variable.

options.text: Each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is the statistic, not a variable.

options.text: The amount of caffeine consumed each day
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: After many months of unrelieved stress, Lia feels worn out and catches one infection after another. Which phase of the general adaptation syndrome is this?

options.why: The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
Correct. The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.
The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.
The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.

questions.explanation: The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features?

options.why: Correct. An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.

questions.explanation: An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.

questions.stem: Alex's inner sense of being a boy has been clear to him since early childhood. Which term describes this inner sense?

options.why: Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.
Correct. Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.
Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.
Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.

questions.explanation: Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: When her usual road is closed, Kim takes a new route home without difficulty because she has a mental picture of the town. This mental picture is which of the following?

options.why: Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.
Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.
Correct. A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.
Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.

questions.explanation: A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.

questions.stem: In which structure of the inner ear do hair cells convert sound vibrations into neural signals?

options.why: Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Correct. The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.explanation: The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.

questions.stem: When a classmate arrives late, Ian decides, 'The bus must have broken down.' Which kind of explanation is this?

options.why: The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.
An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.
Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.
Correct. A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.

questions.explanation: A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: One group differed from the other in the color of the drinks
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The mismatched drinks were served colder than the matching drinks
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: The two groups differed in flavor identification at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge?

options.why: Distress is the negative stress that harms well-being and performance.
Correct. Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.
Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.
A stressor is an event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging.

questions.explanation: Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes emotional stability?

options.text: The Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody
options.why: Correct. This is what emotional stability means.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative
options.why: That describes agreeableness.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined
options.why: That describes conscientiousness.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things
options.why: That describes openness to experience.

questions.explanation: Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: Correct. A negative correlation means the two measures tend to move in opposite directions.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: That would be a positive correlation.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

questions.explanation: A negative correlation means the two measures tend to move in opposite directions.

questions.stem: A theory explains how we hear high-pitched sounds by saying that they stimulate a particular location on the cochlea. Which theory is this?

options.why: Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.
Sensorineural deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the hair cells of the cochlea or to the auditory nerve.
Correct. Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.

questions.explanation: Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: +0.86, −0.78, −0.93, +0.44. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.93 is farthest from zero.
+0.44 is closer to zero.
−0.78 is closer to zero.
+0.86 is closer to zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.93 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes linear perspective?

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer
options.why: That describes interposition.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away
options.why: That describes relative size.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance
options.why: Correct. This is what linear perspective means.

options.text: The monocular depth cue in which hazy objects are seen as farther away than sharp ones
options.why: That describes relative clarity.

questions.explanation: Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.stem: Freud argued that slips of the tongue reveal wishes that people do not know they have. Where did he believe these wishes are held?

options.why: A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.
Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
Correct. The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.

questions.explanation: The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.

questions.stem: Fans rate players on their own team as more skilled and more honest than equally good players on other teams. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.
Correct. In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.explanation: In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes resilience?

options.text: The ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship
options.why: Correct. This is what resilience means.

options.text: The scientific study of the strengths and conditions that help people and communities thrive
options.why: That describes positive psychology.

options.text: The positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person
options.why: That describes signature strengths.

options.text: The positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event
options.why: That describes posttraumatic growth.

questions.explanation: Resilience is the ability to recover and adapt well after stress or hardship.

questions.stem: After hours without water, Tom feels an unpleasant tension that pushes him to find a drink. Which theory of motivation best explains this?

options.why: The Yerkes-Dodson law is the principle that performance is best at a moderate level of arousal.
Incentive theory is the theory that behavior is pulled by rewards from outside the person.
Homeostasis is the body's tendency to keep its internal state, such as temperature, steady.
Correct. Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.

questions.explanation: Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.

questions.stem: Dana pictures the layout of her house to count the windows. Which part of working memory is she using?

options.why: Correct. The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.
Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.

questions.explanation: The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.text: The remembered speed of the cars
options.why: This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes denial?

options.text: The defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality
options.why: Correct. This is what denial means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior
options.why: That describes rationalization.

options.text: The defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one
options.why: That describes displacement.

options.text: The defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people
options.why: That describes projection.

questions.explanation: Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.

questions.stem: Students are 90 percent sure of answers that turn out to be right only 60 percent of the time. Which tendency is this?

options.why: Correct. Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.explanation: Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes aversion therapy?

options.text: The behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus
options.why: Correct. This is what aversion therapy means.

options.text: The technique of using electronic monitoring to show a person their body's signals so that they can learn to control them
options.why: That describes biofeedback.

options.text: A list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening
options.why: That describes a fear hierarchy.

options.text: The behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards
options.why: That describes a token economy.

questions.explanation: Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.

questions.stem: During adolescence, Luis grows facial hair and his voice deepens. These changes are examples of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.
Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.
Puberty is the period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce.
Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.

questions.explanation: Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.

questions.stem: A door swinging open casts a changing image on the retina, yet it still looks rectangular. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.
Correct. Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.
Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.
Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.

questions.explanation: Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the gambler's fallacy?

options.text: The tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it
options.why: That describes the sunk-cost fallacy.

options.text: The activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior
options.why: That describes priming.

options.text: The judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind
options.why: That describes the availability heuristic.

options.text: The mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently
options.why: Correct. This is what the gambler's fallacy means.

questions.explanation: The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.

questions.stem: Critics argue that a so-called creativity test actually measures vocabulary. Which quality are they questioning?

options.why: Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.
Correct. Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.
Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.

questions.explanation: Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.

questions.stem: At twenty-two, Tariq has finished school but still lives with his parents and is exploring career options. Which period of life is he in?

options.why: The personal fable is the belief of adolescents that they are unique and that bad things will not happen to them.
Correct. Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.
Pretend play is the play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations.
Adverse childhood experiences is the stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems.

questions.explanation: Emerging adulthood is the period from about 18 to the mid-twenties, between adolescence and full independence.

questions.stem: To remember the term 'hippocampus', Sol links it to a hippo on a campus who never forgets his classes. Which technique is he using?

options.why: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Correct. Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.text: The type of injection given after drinking
options.why: Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.

options.text: The number of animals in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also test hypotheses.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also use numerical data.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: After the birth of a new baby, a six-year-old starts sucking his thumb and talking like a toddler. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.
Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.
Correct. Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.

questions.explanation: Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.

questions.stem: After solving ten math problems with one formula, Abby keeps trying that formula on a problem that needs a different approach. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Convergent thinking is thinking that narrows the possibilities down to the single best answer.
Correct. A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.
Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.
Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.

questions.explanation: A mental set is the tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise?

options.why: Correct. Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.
Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person restricts food to the point of being dangerously underweight, with an intense fear of gaining weight.

questions.explanation: Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes phonemic encoding?

options.text: The encoding of a word based on its sound
options.why: Correct. This is what phonemic encoding means.

options.text: The encoding of information, such as space, time and frequency, without conscious effort
options.why: That describes automatic processing.

options.text: The encoding that requires attention and conscious effort
options.why: That describes effortful processing.

options.text: The deep encoding of a word based on its meaning
options.why: That describes semantic encoding.

questions.explanation: Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others?

options.why: One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.
Correct. Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.
Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.
A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.

questions.explanation: Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the mesosystem?

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school
options.why: That describes the microsystem.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child
options.why: That describes the chronosystem.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child
options.why: That describes the macrosystem.

options.text: In ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings
options.why: Correct. This is what the mesosystem means.

questions.explanation: The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as an impairment of language caused by brain damage?

options.why: Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Correct. Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.
Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.
Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.

questions.explanation: Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.

questions.stem: Researchers find that a person who collapses is helped more quickly when one person is nearby than when a crowd is nearby. What is this finding called?

options.why: The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.
Correct. The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.

questions.explanation: The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.

questions.stem: The group that studied in six short sessions recalled more words. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The study schedule and long-term retention are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The study schedule caused the difference in long-term retention
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Students who sleep after studying remember more than students who stay awake for the same time. This finding best supports which function of sleep?

options.why: The activation-synthesis theory is the theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep.
The consolidation theory is the theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories.
Correct. Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.
Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.explanation: Memory consolidation is the strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: A psychologist says rates of eating disorders are higher where the culture promotes an extremely thin body ideal. Which perspective is this?

options.why: The evolutionary perspective is the view that disorders involve behaviors that once helped survival but are now harmful.
The behavioral perspective is the view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement.
The psychodynamic perspective is the view that disorders result from unconscious conflicts, often rooted in childhood.
Correct. The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.

questions.explanation: The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.

questions.stem: For a week, a patient sleeps two hours a night, speaks rapidly, starts ten projects and feels invincible. Which state is this?

options.why: Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Correct. Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.
Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.explanation: Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.stem: Too little of one neurotransmitter is linked to the tremors of Parkinson's disease, and too much activity of it is linked to schizophrenia. Which neurotransmitter is this?

options.why: Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.
Substance P is the neurotransmitter that carries pain messages to the brain.
Correct. Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.
GABA is the brain's main inhibitory neurotransmitter.

questions.explanation: Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.

questions.stem: Since his teens, Vic has lied, stolen and hurt people without feeling any guilt or remorse. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Paranoid personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by lasting distrust and suspicion of others.
Avoidant personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by extreme sensitivity to rejection and avoidance of social contact.
Correct. Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.
Histrionic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking.

questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.

questions.stem: A patient's sentences jump between unrelated ideas and become a meaningless string of words. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Correct. Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.
Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.

questions.explanation: Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 64 five-year-old children. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: A patient with severe depression that has not responded to drugs is anesthetized and given a brief electric current that causes a short seizure. Which treatment is this?

options.why: Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.
Correct. Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.
A lobotomy is the now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain.
Transcranial magnetic stimulation is the treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression.

questions.explanation: Electroconvulsive therapy is the treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes mental age?

options.text: The single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks
options.why: That describes general intelligence.

options.text: Originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100
options.why: That describes the intelligence quotient.

options.text: The steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations
options.why: That describes the Flynn effect.

options.text: The level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test
options.why: Correct. This is what mental age means.

questions.explanation: Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 500 and a standard deviation of 20. About what percentage of scores are between 460 and 540?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 95% of scores fall within two standard deviations of the mean.

questions.explanation: About 95% of scores fall within two standard deviations of the mean. (480 and 520 are one standard deviation from the mean; 460 and 540 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of the remembered speed of the cars

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of the remembered speed of the cars.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: The remembered speed of the cars was defined as the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group asked about 'smashed' gave higher speed estimates. On average, the value was 66 for the group asked the question with the word 'smashed' and 51 for the group asked the question with the word 'contacted', and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group asked about 'smashed' gave higher speed estimates. (66 compared with 51).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the wording of the question affects the remembered speed of the cars. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the wording of the question. The finding illustrates the misinformation effect: information received after an event can distort the memory of it.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Heavy social media use can harm teenagers' well-being, especially when it leads them to compare themselves with others.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who limited social media to 30 minutes a day had lower loneliness scores (38) than students who continued as usual (45).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because the study was an experiment with random assignment, so reducing social media use can be said to have caused the lower loneliness. Less time online leaves more time for face-to-face contact, which supports well-being.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source C, many teenagers said they felt worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through upward social comparison and relative deprivation: comparing oneself with people who seem better off lowers self-esteem and satisfaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
